To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

AT1a‐knockout mice exhibit a lean phenotype, increased bone mass and bone turnover with advancing age, are resistant to bone loss induced by ovarian deficiency, and have increased expression of RANKL, SOST, and SDF1α in bone.
AT1a receptor‐deficient mice have an increased bone volume, which is due to a positive regulation of bone formation and bone resorption.

the angiotensine II type Ia receptor (AT1a) has a physiological function in regulating bone remodeling and that AT1a deficiency leads to increased bone turnover, increased bone mass, and resistance to ovariectomy‐induced bone loss.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physiological role of the angiotension II receptor in bone metabolism.
the role of the renin angiotensin system in bone metabolism.
the role of the renin‐ angiotensin system in bone remodeling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AT1 receptor is involved in the control of bone mass and turnover.
the renin angiotensin system is involved in bone remodeling and that AT1a is involved in this process.
the AT1a receptor is a physiologically important modulator of bone mass.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AT1a receptor has a physiologial function in the regulation of bone remodeling.

we have demonstrated that AT1a receptor has a physiological function in the regulation of bone metabolism, and that signaling via the AT1a receptor negatively regulates bone formation and resorption, and bone mass.
we found a new function of RAS in bone remodeling, which is mediated through the AT1a receptor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the renin‐Angiotensin system has a physioglogical function in bone remodeling.
the RAS plays a physiological function in bone remodeling.
the renin-angiotensin-system (RAS) is a physiologic regulator of bone mass.
